item.title: China's longest undersea highway tunnel completes shield tunneling
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Constructors make a safety inspection at the construction site of Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, Oct. 2, 2026. China's longest undersea highway tunnel completed all shield-driven excavation work on Friday as a shield machine reached its designated position at a depth of 105 meters beneath the sea surface in Jiaozhou Bay, eastern China's Shandong Province, according to China Railway Construction Corporation Limited. The Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel will connect Qingdao's main urban area with the Qingdao West Coast New Area. The latter is a national-level new area. The 17.48-km project includes a 14.37-km main tunnel section, featuring two main tunnels and a middle service tunnel, with three lanes in each direction and a design speed of 80 km per hour. (Xinhua/Li Ziheng) BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- China's longest undersea highway tunnel completed all shield-driven excavation work on Friday as a shield machine reached its designated position at a depth of 105 meters beneath the sea surface in Jiaozhou Bay, eastern China's Shandong Province, according to China Railway Construction Corporation Limited. The Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel will connect Qingdao's main urban area with the Qingdao West Coast New Area. The latter is a national-level new area. The 17.48-km project includes a 14.37-km main tunnel section, featuring two main tunnels and a middle service tunnel, with three lanes in each direction and a design speed of 80 km per hour. According to Wang Junping with the China Railway 14th Bureau Group Corporation Limited, the project used a combination of drill-and-blast and shield tunneling methods, advancing from both the east and west shores of Jiaozhou Bay and meeting under the sea. The main shield section has a maximum depth of 95 meters below the sea surface, and the service tunnel reaches 105 meters, creating high water pressure and requiring stringent sealing and waterproofing. The team, for the first time, adopted a new muck discharge system, integrating a screw conveyor, rock crusher box and rock crusher, to improve efficiency and reduce blockage risks, Wang said, adding that innovative anti-vibration technology was developed for the shield body to improve stability. Once completed, the new tunnel will help Qingdao form a multi-level cross-bay transport network together with the existing Jiaozhou Bay Tunnel, Jiaozhou Bay Bridge and Jiaozhou Bay Highway. China has issued a plan to comprehensively advance the high-quality development of integrated transport services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the Ministry of Transport announced in July this year. The plan aims to largely establish a modern integrated transport service system by 2030. Under the plan, China will improve connections among different modes of transport, make passenger transfers more convenient and enhance freight logistics services. It will also promote the integration of transport and tourism, improve services at transport hubs, and strengthen rural passenger transport, freight and delivery services. ■ A constructor makes a safety inspection at the construction site of Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, Oct. 2, 2026. item.title: Why global travelers flock to China with empty suitcases
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
* With "China Haul" emerging as a buzz hashtag on social media platforms worldwide, more foreign visitors are flocking to the country not merely for sightseeing, but also for shopping sprees. * In the first seven months of 2026, people from overseas spent 263.6 billion yuan (about 39 billion U.S. dollars) in China, an increase of 27.8 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. * Official data showed that foreign nationals made almost 61.29 million border crossings in the January-August period of 2026, up 19.5 percent from a year earlier. Visa-free entries accounted for 23.72 million of the total, an increase of 26.8 percent compared with 2025. BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- Andrea Triboldi, an Italian tourist, arrived in China with a long shopping list. After landing in Shenzhen, a thriving tech hub in southern China, Triboldi and his 11-year-old son couldn't wait to visit a major sci-tech exhibition, which showcased drones and other latest tech products of this city in Guangdong Province. Prior to the trip, Triboldi had drawn up a shopping list featuring more than 20 Chinese products. "I chose Shenzhen as the first station of our China travel because of its technology. My son is particularly into DJI drones and wants to buy one to take home," he said. Triboldi is not alone. With "China Haul" emerging as a buzz hashtag on social media platforms worldwide, more foreign visitors are flocking to the country not merely for sightseeing, but also for shopping sprees. In the first seven months of 2026, people from overseas spent 263.6 billion yuan (about 39 billion U.S. dollars) in China, an increase of 27.8 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. DIVERSE SHOPPING SPREES "I came here to feel the best technology I have ever seen in the whole world. It's really amazing. We don't have these kinds of drones in Mexico," said Ulises Padilla, an 11-year-old Mexican tourist, in describing his impressions of Shenzhen. The city is drawing an increasing number of foreign visitors like Padilla. An average of nearly 8,000 foreign buyers have visited Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's mega electronics marketplace, each day this year. From January through July, sales of artificial intelligence (AI) products surged more than 55 percent from a year earlier in this area. Sales of AI glasses doubled, while sales of drones and robots climbed by 60 to 70 percent during the same period. Zhang Linwan, an employee of INNO100, a Shenzhen store featuring tech products, said that foreign tourists contribute roughly 40 percent of the store's total sales. "They show strong interest in exoskeletons, 3D printers and laser engraving machines. At our store, they can also make their own 3D dolls and turn photos of themselves and their families into fridge magnets," the employee added. Wang Linlin, who works at a DJI flagship store in Shenzhen, described a similar scene. "We've seen a large number of foreign customers recently. They enjoy getting hands-on experience with our products, especially trying out our drones in test flights," Wang revealed. In Changsha, capital of central China's Hunan Province, Chinese snacks are proving a big hit with foreign tourists. Ivan, a 32-year-old Russian tourist, made a point of visiting Snack Kingdom, a specialty store in the city that offers over 35,000 types of snacks. He said that not many large snack stores in Russia have such a complete range of products, and the variety is so rich that it's a bit difficult to choose. Tanzanian tourist Shija Theodora Desderi commented that the store serves not only as a shopping destination but also as a place for entertainment. She compared Chinese snacks with Tanzanian ones, which she described as sweeter, noting that the former taste refreshing and are more organic, containing less sugar and salt. "From sneakers and cosmetics to trendy toys and daily necessities, my family and friends often have their shopping plans ready before visiting China," said Mok Jin Jin from Malaysia. She said her mother especially likes a Chinese-made blender and often uses it to make various healthy drinks for the family. The machine's one-touch automatic cleaning feature is particularly appealing, sparing her the hassle of manual cleaning. APPEALING PRODUCTS PLUS FAVORABLE POLICIES It is not only the price advantage, but the design, quality and practicality of Chinese products that draw the attention of foreign tourists, according to the Malaysian. She concluded that behind the "China Haul" phenomenon lies not only China's enhanced manufacturing capabilities, but also profound shifts in Chinese brand design, innovation and consumer experience. Carlos Alvarado, an international student from Guatemala, is already a seasoned shopper in China. "Chinese products, like clothes, accessories and daily necessities, are not only competitively priced, but also feature trendy designs that are hard to find in stores in my home country," he said. Moreover, an array of favorable policies, such as visa-free policies and departure tax refunds, has further boosted the shopping frenzy in China. Official data showed that foreign nationals made almost 61.29 million border crossings in the January-August period of 2026, up 19.5 percent from a year earlier. Visa-free entries accounted for 23.72 million of the total, an increase of 26.8 percent compared with 2025. Before ending her trip to Chengdu, capital city of southwest China's Sichuan Province, Hungarian tourist Annamaria purchased some tea, teacups and teapots as gifts for her mother and younger brother at home. "I like shopping in China because it's very convenient and there are many choices here," she said, praising the tax refund policy for allowing her to get refunds immediately upon purchase. "The policy has boosted our sales. Foreign tourists now account for 30 percent of our daily customer flow," said Zhou Man, manager of a Chengdu store of Xiaomi, a Chinese consumer electronics and technology company. Data from the Ministry of Commerce revealed that the number of overseas visitors applying for departure tax refunds had increased by more than threefold year on year during the first seven months of 2026. Roger Matute, an international student from Honduras, was impressed by how convenient mobile payment is in China. "I have rarely used cash since I arrived here because it is very easy to pay everything with my smartphone using WeChat or Alipay apps," he said. A range of favorable conditions, including tax refunds, mobile payments and visa-free policies, have systematically reduced the cost of cross-border consumer transactions, helping to facilitate the "China Haul" trend, according to Gao Li, vice dean of the School of International Business, Tianjin Foreign Studies University, located in north China. The popularity of "China Haul" essentially stems from a shift in the consumption logic of overseas tourists, who are moving from purchasing foreign cultural symbols to buying Chinese technologies, designs and consumption experiences, said He Yun, an associate professor at the school of public administration of central China's Hunan University. The trend, she noted, is underpinned by the upgrading of China's manufacturing and cultural and creative industries, a substantial transition from exporting production capacity to exporting brands and lifestyles. (Video reporters: Hu Rong and Zhang Yujie; Video editors: Hong Liang, Zhu Cong and Zhou Yang) ■

item.title: SW China's Village Super League hosts a "World Cup" of its own
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
GUIYANG, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- When foreign players marched past the stands at the Village Super League (VSL) football field, it drove home for many in Rongjiang County that the "World Cup" they had long dreamed of was finally happening. The grassroots VSL, known in Chinese as "Cun Chao," originated in Rongjiang County, Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, southwest China's Guizhou Province, and has been running for more than three years. The opening ceremony of the 2026 VSL International Football Cup was held at the VSL field in the county on Thursday evening, attracting a total of 371 players from 16 teams representing more than 30 countries and regions, including 199 foreign players, who took part in the parade. Yang Bing, the evening's commentator, said excitedly, "The 2026 Mini Cun Chao World Cup opened today. Rongjiang has truly turned a county-level village tournament into a global one." Since going viral from May to July 2023, the VSL has pursued the goal of "attracting people from all over the world to play together." It plans to hold the Mini Cun Chao World Cup in 2026 and the Cun Chao World Cup in 2028. The 2026 international tournament is the so-called Mini Cun Chao World Cup. Yang, a native of Kouzhai Village in Rongjiang County and a lifelong football fan, has commented on hundreds of VSL matches, including many international friendlies. He said that this international football cup is different. It is the first time the VSL has hosted an international cup, making his dream of a Mini Cun Chao World Cup a reality. When 14-year-old Yang Zheng, a football fan from Rongjiang, saw foreign teams from Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and elsewhere at the field, he could not help exclaiming, "A Mini Cun Chao World Cup is really being held in my hometown!" "The Brazil team also came to Rongjiang during last year's National Day holiday. They were unbeaten in all their matches, so I am very curious about their performance this year," said Yang Zheng, who has played football for four years. He added that he was delighted and inspired to see players from around the world compete in his hometown and hoped to play on the VSL international stage himself one day. "Since the VSL went viral, I have played in the first two international tournaments, but this is the one with the most foreign teams and players I have ever seen," said Lu Jinfu. He played for the Rongjiang County team against Malaysia South Tigers that evening and felt the same sense of excitement. Lu was once an energetic teenager on the pitch and has now grown into a calm veteran. "Walking along the sideline, I heard different languages. It really felt like walking into a World Cup stadium. I was very excited," Lu said. "This is the Mini Cun Chao World Cup!" said Jiang Zuoxian, a VSL ambassador, noting that the seven-day competition began on September 30. She has been at the pitch since the first day to watch and cheer for the teams. On the morning of October 1, when Jiang saw Mateus Pereira, a Brazilian player who had visited Rongjiang before, she taught him to sing a Miao folk song. She hummed slowly, line by line, and Pereira imitated her with gestures. "Language barriers do not matter. Players come to the VSL not just for matches, but also for fun," Jiang said, adding that football has no borders and sincerity is the most touching. "We admire their skills, and they love our way of life. This mutual affinity has made us good friends." As old friends of the VSL, the Brazilian players enjoy the football and cultural atmosphere each time. Off the pitch, they took photos with tourists and cheered for other teams. On the pitch, they won applause with their samba style. "The VSL international tournament has the best atmosphere of any amateur international football match I have ever seen," said Akonjom Great Nek, a Brazilian player whose Chinese name is Kang Wei. "Many players from different countries came to this tournament," said Nek, adding that the international football cup really feels like a Mini World Cup, through which he has made many friends and had pleasant conversations with them. "This is the charm of football," said Nek, emphasizing that it brings people from all over the world together to understand each other, share joy and build consensus. It also made Nek look forward to the 2028 Cun Chao World Cup, and he hoped to participate and experience an even more enthusiastic football atmosphere. Yang added that more and more foreign teams have come to Rongjiang to play in recent years, gradually turning the VSL pitch into a major platform for people-to-people exchanges between China and the rest of the world. ■

item.title: A more stable U.S.-China relationship matters for the world, says U.S. expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
NEW YORK, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- A more stable U.S.-China relationship has effects well beyond the bilateral relationship because the two countries are deeply connected to the global economy and play major roles in international institutions and global governance, a renowned U.S. expert on China affairs has said. In a written interview with Xinhua, Denis Simon, former senior adviser for China affairs to the president of Duke University, noted that Chinese President Xi Jinping said during the recent state visit to the United States that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, complement each other and benefit the world. "I read this as an attempt to frame the relationship in terms of mutual national interests rather than as a zero-sum contest. Both China and the United States have their own national ambitions and domestic priorities, but those objectives do not necessarily require the other country to fail," said Simon, who also served as executive vice chancellor of Duke Kunshan University in 2015-2020. "Rather than asking either side to abandon its own national goals, the message is that China's development and America's prosperity can coexist and, under the right conditions, reinforce one another," he said. Regarding the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences and promises of peace, Simon described the formulation as "an effort to provide a practical framework for managing a relationship in which competition is unavoidable but conflict is not inevitable." "The key phrase for me is 'competition within bounds.' It recognizes that China and the United States will compete in areas such as technology, trade and strategic influence. The objective is not necessarily to eliminate that competition, but to establish boundaries so that competition does not become confrontation," he said. Simon said "manageable differences" acknowledges that some disagreements may be very difficult to resolve in the foreseeable future. A stable relationship, therefore, cannot depend on resolving every difference. "It needs mechanisms that allow the two sides to disagree without allowing individual disputes to destabilize the entire relationship," he said. "If implemented consistently, the framework could shift the emphasis from trying to eliminate competition toward making competition predictable and manageable, while expanding cooperation wherever interests genuinely overlap." Simon identified economic and trade issues as an obvious area where concrete progress could have immediate effects, while noting that technology and supply-chain questions are more difficult "because they involve both economic and national-security considerations." "But precisely for that reason, they require sustained dialogue and clearer communication," he said, adding that beyond bilateral issues, cooperation on climate, energy, public health and other transnational challenges could demonstrate that competition does not have to prevent practical collaboration.■

item.title: Crime drama inspired by renowned trace-evidence expert leads China's holiday box office
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
by Xinhua writers Zhang Yunlong and Zhang Xiyue BEIJING/HARBIN, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- Crime drama "Traces of Justice" led China's box office on Thursday, the first day of the weeklong National Day holiday, emerging as the early front-runner in a release calendar short on traditional blockbuster fare. According to ticketing platform Maoyan, China's box office totaled 180 million yuan (about 26.73 million U.S. dollars) on Oct. 1. "Traces of Justice" generated 71 million yuan, accounting for 39 percent of total ticket sales. The film was followed by comedy "Mr. & Mrs. Pardon," which earned 48 million yuan. Together, the two titles accounted for nearly 66 percent of opening-day revenue. Directed and co-written by Chen Sicheng, "Traces of Justice" is based on the life and work of Cui Daozhi, a renowned trace-evidence expert. The film stars Zhang Yi as Cui Xun, a trace-evidence specialist, alongside Ma Li as a forensic pathologist and Chen Minghao as a veteran detective. Rather than focusing on action-driven police work, the film centers on forensic science and evidence analysis. Drawing inspiration from a series of real criminal cases dating back to the 1970s, it follows investigators solving seemingly unsolvable crimes through bite marks, fingerprints, fibers, firearms evidence and other overlooked clues. The story traces the development of Chinese forensic techniques over several decades. The film's strong opening suggests audiences may be responding to a genre mix that differs from the patriotic epics and effects-heavy spectacles that have often dominated China's National Day holiday in recent years. Maoyan analyst Lai Li noted that this year's National Day lineup offers a broad range of genres but lacks a clear tentpole release capable of driving the market on its own. That dynamic may have worked in favor of "Traces of Justice," which entered the holiday with recognizable creative talent and a distinctive crime-investigation premise. The film kicked off its nationwide roadshow Thursday in Harbin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, where Cui spent much of his professional life and where portions of the story are set. Cui joined the provincial public security department in 1955 and has spent more than six decades working in criminal forensic science, participating in over 1,200 major cases and examining thousands of pieces of evidence. Director Chen said Cui's life story offered a unique lens through which to examine the evolution of Chinese criminal investigation. Star Zhang Yi described the film as not only a portrait of one investigator but also a tribute to generations of police officers whose work has largely remained out of public view. Whether "Traces of Justice" can maintain its lead over the remainder of the seven-day break remains an open question. The market is expected to become more competitive as additional titles are released, including crime sequel "Go for Broke 2" on Oct. 3 and imported horror title "Resident Evil" on Oct. 5. These staggered openings, along with sustained demand for family moviegoing during the holiday, are expected to support the market throughout the latter half of the holiday period, according to Chen Jin, an analyst at film data platform Beacon. ■

item.title: China's railway passenger trips hit record single-day high
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 25.204 million passenger trips on Oct. 1, the first day of the week-long National Day holiday, setting a new single-day record, China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway) said Friday. On Oct. 2, the railway network is expected to handle 20.39 million passenger trips, with 1,462 additional trains scheduled to accommodate the high demand, the company said. Passenger ticket pre-sales show that Friday's popular departure cities include Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Chengdu, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Wuhan, Xi'an, Zhengzhou and Nanjing, while popular arrival cities include Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Hangzhou, Shanghai, Wuhan, Xi'an, Zhengzhou, Nanjing and Changsha. Routes such as Xi'an-Chengdu round trips, as well as Beijing to Shenyang, Zhengzhou and Qingdao, are among the busiest. Railway authorities across the country have strengthened transport organization and implemented measures to ensure safe, convenient and comfortable travel. The China Railway Taiyuan Group has coordinated with local transport departments and scenic spots to add shuttle buses linking Datong South Station with the Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site featuring over 50,000 Buddhist stone sculptures, and the Hengshan Mountain scenic area in north China's Shanxi Province. The China Railway Hohhot Group has added 11 multiple-unit trains on the Baotou-Wuhai section of the Baotou-Yinchuan high-speed railway. The China Railway Wuhan Group, tapping the newly opened Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway, has launched a promotion campaign with local governments in Yichang and Xingshan, offering passengers exclusive discounts at scenic spots, hotels and homestays with their train tickets. China Railway expects some 284 million passenger trips during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period, which extends from Sept. 23 to Oct. 8. On Oct. 1, a total of 329.5 million cross-regional passenger trips were made across China, down 1.9 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Transport. Specifically, railway passenger trips reached 25.204 million, up 9 percent year on year; road passenger trips stood at 300.36 million, down 2.8 percent; waterway passenger trips totaled 1.416 million, up 7.2 percent; and civil aviation passenger trips came in at 2.515 million, up 0.5 percent, according to the ministry. China's total cross-regional passenger trips are expected to reach 308.19 million on Oct. 2, up 2.1 percent year on year, the ministry added. On Friday, the National Energy Administration reported that, based on statistical analysis of 62,700 highway charging facilities included in the national charging infrastructure monitoring service platform, the first day of the National Day holiday saw a total highway charging volume of 28.05 million kilowatt-hours nationwide. This represents a 60.4 percent increase compared to the first day of last year's National Day holiday, setting a new single-day holiday record for charging volume. ■

item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. China's National Day falls on Oct. 1. Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China." He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said. Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy. He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added. He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification. China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said. ■ The Communist Party of China and state leaders Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attend a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China along with around 800 guests at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026.
